sources.title: Informe Anual 2024: Ingreso de visitantes a las áreas protegidas de Galápagos
sources.proves: 279,277 Galápagos tourist arrivals in 2024; 55% foreign and 45% national; 79% land-based and 21% cruise-based visitor mode; 55% arrived through Baltra and 45% through San Cristóbal.

sources.title: Transporte entre islas pobladas
sources.proves: Passenger launches of up to 20 people operate from the main pier of each populated port; typical trip time 2–3 hours; $30 per person per route; January–June has calmer seas than July–December; lists Santa Cruz–San Cristóbal, Santa Cruz–Isabela and Santa Cruz–Floreana schedules, with Floreana Tuesday/Thursday.

sources.title: Subsecretaría de Puertos norma actividad de taxis acuáticos en Galápagos
sources.publisher: Ministerio de Infraestructura y Transporte (formerly MTOP)
sources.proves: Resolution 0032 regulates public maritime passenger transport, including routes at Puerto Baquerizo Moreno, Puerto Ayora, Puerto Villamil and Puerto Velasco Ibarra, plus operating limits; this is regulatory context, not proof of current fare beyond the newer DPNG page.

sources.title: Official travel report: Muelle Gus Angermeyer to Puerto Baquerizo Moreno
sources.publisher: Consejo de Gobierno del Régimen Especial de Galápagos
sources.proves: Names Muelle Gus Angermeyer and records a 15:00 maritime departure to Puerto Baquerizo Moreno with 17:00 arrival.

sources.title: Official travel report: Puerto Villamil–Puerto Ayora
sources.publisher: Agencia de Regulación y Control de la Bioseguridad y Cuarentena para Galápagos (ABG)
sources.proves: Records transfer to the passenger pier and a 15:00–17:00 Puerto Villamil–Puerto Ayora maritime trip.

sources.title: Official travel report: Muelle Tiburón Martillo
sources.publisher: Agencia de Regulación y Control de la Bioseguridad y Cuarentena para Galápagos (ABG)
sources.proves: Names Muelle Tiburón Martillo as the inspection point for passenger baggage and cargo bound to other populated ports.

sources.title: Official travel report: inauguration of tourism and cargo pier at Puerto Velasco Ibarra
sources.publisher: Consejo de Gobierno del Régimen Especial de Galápagos
sources.proves: Names the tourism and cargo pier at Puerto Velasco Ibarra, Floreana, and records its inauguration context.

sources.title: Desarrollo sostenible del turismo basado en bellezas naturales y arqueológicas
sources.proves: Ica recorded 1,119,437 visits to principal tourist sites, 1,657,046 lodging arrivals, and 2,194,261 overnight stays in 2024; these are broad regional flows, not corridor passengers.

sources.title: Reserva Nacional SIIPG – Islas Ballestas
sources.publisher: Servicio Nacional de Áreas Naturales Protegidas por el Estado (SERNANP)
sources.proves: Ballestas is open Monday–Sunday 06:00–13:00, year-round; Paracas–Ballestas is 21.4 km and 1h40 round trip; national adult ANP entry is S/11, local adult S/5, combined Paracas/Ballestas promotional entry S/17; no SERNANP-authorized operator list is currently published.

sources.title: Tour Islas Ballestas desde Paracas
sources.proves: Advertised operator fare of S/40 per person regular and S/60 on specified holidays; this is not a regulated tariff and should be re-quoted before finance use.

sources.title: Plan Regional de Desarrollo Turístico de Ica
sources.proves: Reports five artisanal fishing landing places in the area and that one in Paracas is used to embark tourists to Islas Ballestas; supports El Chaco tourist-boarding function but not a coordinate.

sources.title: Islas Cavinzas e Islotes Palomino – Reserva Nacional SIIPG
sources.proves: Official access guidance identifies Callao Muelle Plaza Grau / Marina Club as the maritime departure area for Palomino.

sources.title: Estos son los lugares que puedes conocer en el Día del Turismo Chalaco
sources.proves: States that small launches depart Muelle Dársena for coastal tours; supports a verified tourist departure function.

sources.title: Anexo 1 – Lista de terminales portuarios y embarcaderos que conforman el SPN y su clasificación
sources.proves: Provides the official national port/landing-facility classification baseline; facility listing alone does not prove public passenger service.

sources.title: Terminal Portuario General San Martín – Paracas, Pisco
sources.proves: Describes regulated multipurpose commercial cargo terminal services; it does not establish a public passenger boarding point.

sources.title: PRODUCE: expediente técnico para rehabilitación temporal del muelle marginal del DPA San Andrés
sources.proves: Confirms the Desembarcadero Pesquero Artesanal de San Andrés exists and had a marginal-pier rehabilitation process; it does not prove public passenger authorization or present operational status.

sources.title: DiDi Global
sources.proves: Country-level DiDi presence in Ecuador and Peru only; no city/pier-level binding for the researched geographies.

partner_narrative_notes.placement: Separate DiDi proposal overlay only; do not insert into canonical city briefs.
positioning: Galápagos is a regulated, conservation-sensitive, port-to-door coordination problem, not an unrestricted mobility market. Frame DiDi as timed first/last-mile orchestration around authority-published launches, with no implication of DiDi boat operations or confirmed local rideshare coverage.

Santa Cruz is the operational interchange; Isabela and San Cristóbal are daily links, while Floreana is a lower-frequency Tuesday/Thursday link. Use the official $30 fare and 2–3-hour duration only as current traveler context, not Navier revenue or demand.
The 279,277 annual visitor total is an archipelago TAM signal. Never map it directly to route riders; use a bottom-up manifest/occupancy model after route-stamp repair.

Peru should split proven excursion gateways (Callao–Palomino and Paracas–Ballestas) from speculative intercity coastal links. The strongest near-term proposal story is dispatch, ticketing handoff and timed ground transfer at verified excursion origins.

Pisco/San Andrés is a research/permission lane, not a sellable passenger route today. The fishing landing and commercial General San Martín terminal must not be represented as public passenger piers without APN/Capitanía/operator confirmation.
Country-level DiDi presence supports a partnership conversation but not city-level availability claims in Galápagos, Paracas or Pisco.
